authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed DDoS-to-Benign prediction rates were higher in the plain attack branch than the paired clean branch; the defended branch reduced the plain-attack mean rate. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance relative to the paired preattack reference.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.191026, versus 0.056499 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.094131, an absolute reduction of 0.096894 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.860237 to 0.520150, with recovery fraction 0.395341.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to claim verified malicious intent; the supplied evidence does not establish it.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery; oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and not substituted.
Refuse to make client-flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decisions.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
